/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)

The Hadwiger conjecture relates the chromatic number of a graph to its clique minors: if a
finite loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, every graph $G$
satisfies $\chi(G) \le h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$ (the largest $t$ such
that $K_t$ is a minor of $G$).

The conjecture was made by Hadwiger in 1943 [Ha43]. It is known for $t \le 6$; the case $t = 5$
is equivalent to the four color theorem (Wagner, 1937) and the case $t = 6$ was proved by
Robertson, Seymour and Thomas [RST93]. It is open for every $t > 6$.

Mathlib has no notion of graph minor, so this file defines one via branch sets (minor models).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Ha43] Hadwiger, H., *Über eine Klassifikation der Streckenkomplexe*. Vierteljschr.
  Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich 88 (1943), 133–142.
- [RST93] Robertson, N., Seymour, P. and Thomas, R., *Hadwiger's conjecture for $K_6$-free
  graphs*. Combinatorica 13 (1993), 279–361.
-/

blocks.docstring:
A graph `H` is a *minor* of a graph `G` if `G` contains a model of `H`: a family of pairwise
disjoint vertex sets `f w` of `G` (the *branch sets*), one for each vertex `w` of `H`, such that
every branch set induces a connected (in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, and whenever
`w₁` and `w₂` are adjacent in `H` some vertex of `f w₁` is adjacent in `G` to some vertex of
`f w₂`.

Equivalently, `H` is isomorphic to a graph obtained from a subgraph of `G` by contracting edges
(each branch set is contracted to a single vertex).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Matroid.IsMinor (matroids, not graphs); SimpleGraph.Subgraph / SimpleGraph.induce with Connected (used as building blocks); SimpleGraph.Subgraph.Connected. None expresses edge contraction/minor containment.
justification.name: HadwigerConjecture2.IsMinor
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has any notion of a graph minor (only Matroid.IsMinor exists). Defined via the standard model/branch-set characterization: H is a minor of G iff there is a family f : W → Set V of pairwise disjoint vertex sets, each inducing a connected (hence nonempty) subgraph of G, with an edge of G between f w₁ and f w₂ whenever w₁ ~ w₂ in H. This is equivalent (Diestel, Ch. 1.7) to H being isomorphic to a graph obtained from a subgraph of G by edge contractions. Five short proved API lemmas exercise it: reflexivity, monotonicity in G, K_0 is a minor of everything, K_1 minor ↔ Nonempty V, K_2 minor ↔ G has an edge.

blocks.text:
/--
A graph `H` is a *minor* of a graph `G` if `G` contains a model of `H`: a family of pairwise
disjoint vertex sets `f w` of `G` (the *branch sets*), one for each vertex `w` of `H`, such that
every branch set induces a connected (in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, and whenever
`w₁` and `w₂` are adjacent in `H` some vertex of `f w₁` is adjacent in `G` to some vertex of
`f w₂`.

Equivalently, `H` is isomorphic to a graph obtained from a subgraph of `G` by contracting edges
(each branch set is contracted to a single vertex).
-/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (f w)).Connected) ∧
    (Pairwise fun w₁ w₂ => Disjoint (f w₁) (f w₂)) ∧
    ∀ w₁ w₂, H.Adj w₁ w₂ → ∃ v₁ ∈ f w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ f w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G :=
  ⟨fun v => {v}, fun v => by simp, fun v w hvw => by simpa,
    fun v w h => ⟨v, rfl, w, rfl, h⟩⟩

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.of_le {K : SimpleGraph W} {G G' : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G ≤ G')
    (h : IsMinor K G) : IsMinor K G' := by
  obtain ⟨f, hconn, hdisj, hadj⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, fun w => (hconn w).mono fun _ _ h => hG h, hdisj, fun w₁ w₂ hw => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨v₁, hv₁, v₂, hv₂, hv⟩ := hadj w₁ w₂ hw
  exact ⟨v₁, hv₁, v₂, hv₂, hG hv⟩

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_one_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 1)) G ↔ Nonempty V := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hf, -, -⟩
    obtain ⟨⟨v, -⟩⟩ := (hf 0).nonempty
    exact ⟨v⟩
  · rintro ⟨v⟩
    refine ⟨fun _ => {v}, fun _ => by simp, fun i j hij => (hij (Subsingleton.elim i j)).elim,
      fun i j h => ?_⟩
    exact absurd (Subsingleton.elim i j) h.ne

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_two_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 2)) G ↔ ∃ v w, G.Adj v w := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, -, -, hadj⟩
    obtain ⟨v, -, w, -, hvw⟩ := hadj 0 1 (by decide)
    exact ⟨v, w, hvw⟩
  · rintro ⟨v, w, hvw⟩
    refine ⟨![{v}, {w}], fun i => by fin_cases i <;> simp, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro i j hij
      fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [hvw.ne, hvw.ne.symm]
    · intro i j hij
      fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [hvw.symm]

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem not_isMinor_completeGraph_of_card_lt [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) {t : ℕ}
    (ht : Fintype.card V < t) : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G := by
  rintro ⟨B, hconn, hdisj, -⟩
  have hne : ∀ i, (B i).Nonempty := fun i =>
    Set.nonempty_coe_sort.mp (hconn i).nonempty
  choose f hf using hne
  have hinj : Function.Injective f := fun i j hij => by
    by_contra hne
    exact Set.disjoint_left.mp (hdisj hne) (hf i) (hij ▸ hf j)
  have := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hinj
  simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at this
  omega
blocks.docstring: A graph with fewer than `t` vertices has no `K_t` minor.

blocks.docstring:
**Hadwiger conjecture.** For every finite loopless graph $G$ and every positive integer $t$, if
$G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$.

Equivalently, if every proper coloring of $G$ uses at least $k$ colors, then $G$ contains $k$
pairwise disjoint connected subgraphs such that each pair of them is joined by an edge, i.e. $G$
has a $K_k$ minor. In algebraic form: $\chi(G) \le h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of
$G$ (the largest $k$ such that $K_k$ is a minor of $G$).

A `SimpleGraph` is loopless by definition, and parallel edges affect neither the chromatic number
nor the existence of a $K_t$ minor. The case $t = 0$ is degenerate: $K_0$ is a minor of every
graph (`isMinor_completeGraph_zero`).

claims.decomposer_note: The single Prop: for every finite loopless (simple) graph G and every positive integer t, if G has no K_t minor then χ(G) < t (equivalently χ(G) ≤ h(G), the Hadwiger number); it should be stated for finite graphs, needs a bespoke graph-minor definition since Mathlib has none, t = 0 is degenerate (every graph has a K_0 minor, and Wikipedia's range 1 ≤ t reflects this), and the article's equivalent forms are reformulations of this same statement rather than separate questions, while the Hajós/list/odd/linear variants it discusses are not referred to by the list entry.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful Prop (finite SimpleGraph G, K_t minor via branch-set model: pairwise disjoint, connected (hence nonempty) branch sets with an edge between every pair of adjacent H-vertices; conclusion G.chromaticNumber < (t : ℕ∞)). Checked against the article lead ('if G is loopless and has no K_t minor then χ(G) < t'): direction of implication, strict bound, finiteness, and the t = 0 boundary (K_0 is a minor of every graph, so the case is vacuous) are all correct; t = 1 boundary verified in a scratch file (no K_1 minor ⇔ V empty ⇒ χ = 0 < 1). c07 chosen as base for its generic reusable `IsMinor H G` (literally 'H is a minor of G', as in the source) with a good set of API/test lemmas (refl, monotonicity under subgraph, K_0/K_1/K_2 characterizations). Edits: added the explicit `0 < t` hypothesis (as in c03/c04/c05/c08 and the decomposition note 'every positive integer t'; logically redundant but matches the source's range 1 ≤ t), added c06's `not_isMinor_completeGraph_of_card_lt` API lemma, retagged the K_0/K_1/K_2 lemmas as `test`, and dropped the non-slot `research solved` variant `le_six` since the final file should contain exactly the surviving slots.

context:
In graph theory, the Hadwiger conjecture states that if $G$ is loopless and has no $K_{t}$ minor then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi (G)<t$. It is known to be true for $1\leq t\leq 6$. The conjecture is a generalization of the four color theorem and is considered to be one of the most important and challenging open problems in the field.
Reversing the implication, the conjecture can equivalently be stated in the following form. According to it, if all proper colorings of an undirected graph $G$ use $k$ or more colors, then one can find $k$ disjoint connected subgraphs of $G$ such that each subgraph is connected by an edge to each other subgraph. Contracting the edges within each of these subgraphs so that each subgraph collapses to a single vertex produces a complete graph $K_{k}$ on $k$ vertices as a minor of $G$.
The conjecture was made by Hugo Hadwiger in 1943. Bollobás, Catlin & Erdős (1980) call it "one of the deepest unsolved problems in graph theory".

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition is right: the article's 'equivalent forms' are reformulations of the same Prop, and the Hajós, list-coloring, odd-minor and linear variants are distinct conjectures not referred to by the list entry.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)

The Hadwiger conjecture relates the chromatic number of a graph to its clique minors: if a
finite loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, every graph $G$
satisfies $\chi(G) \le h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$ (the largest $t$ such
that $K_t$ is a minor of $G$).

The conjecture was made by Hadwiger in 1943 [Ha43]. It is known for $t \le 6$; the case $t = 5$
is equivalent to the four color theorem (Wagner, 1937) and the case $t = 6$ was proved by
Robertson, Seymour and Thomas [RST93]. It is open for every $t > 6$.

Mathlib has no notion of graph minor, so this file defines one via branch sets (minor models).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Ha43] Hadwiger, H., *Über eine Klassifikation der Streckenkomplexe*. Vierteljschr.
  Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich 88 (1943), 133–142.
- [RST93] Robertson, N., Seymour, P. and Thomas, R., *Hadwiger's conjecture for $K_6$-free
  graphs*. Combinatorica 13 (1993), 279–361.
-/

namespace HadwigerConjecture2

open SimpleGraph

variable {V W : Type*}

/--
A graph `H` is a *minor* of a graph `G` if `G` contains a model of `H`: a family of pairwise
disjoint vertex sets `f w` of `G` (the *branch sets*), one for each vertex `w` of `H`, such that
every branch set induces a connected (in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, and whenever
`w₁` and `w₂` are adjacent in `H` some vertex of `f w₁` is adjacent in `G` to some vertex of
`f w₂`.

Equivalently, `H` is isomorphic to a graph obtained from a subgraph of `G` by contracting edges
(each branch set is contracted to a single vertex).
-/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (f w)).Connected) ∧
    (Pairwise fun w₁ w₂ => Disjoint (f w₁) (f w₂)) ∧
    ∀ w₁ w₂, H.Adj w₁ w₂ → ∃ v₁ ∈ f w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ f w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself: take every branch set to be a single vertex. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G :=
  ⟨fun v => {v}, fun v => by simp, fun v w hvw => by simpa,
    fun v w h => ⟨v, rfl, w, rfl, h⟩⟩

/-- A minor of a subgraph of `G` is a minor of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.of_le {K : SimpleGraph W} {G G' : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G ≤ G')
    (h : IsMinor K G) : IsMinor K G' := by
  obtain ⟨f, hconn, hdisj, hadj⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, fun w => (hconn w).mono fun _ _ h => hG h, hdisj, fun w₁ w₂ hw => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨v₁, hv₁, v₂, hv₂, hv⟩ := hadj w₁ w₂ hw
  exact ⟨v₁, hv₁, v₂, hv₂, hG hv⟩

/--
The complete graph on zero vertices is a minor of every graph. In particular the case $t = 0$
of the Hadwiger conjecture holds vacuously.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_zero (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 0)) G :=
  ⟨Fin.elim0, fun w => w.elim0, fun w => w.elim0, fun w => w.elim0⟩

/-- A graph has a $K_1$ minor if and only if it has a vertex. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_one_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 1)) G ↔ Nonempty V := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hf, -, -⟩
    obtain ⟨⟨v, -⟩⟩ := (hf 0).nonempty
    exact ⟨v⟩
  · rintro ⟨v⟩
    refine ⟨fun _ => {v}, fun _ => by simp, fun i j hij => (hij (Subsingleton.elim i j)).elim,
      fun i j h => ?_⟩
    exact absurd (Subsingleton.elim i j) h.ne

/-- A graph has a $K_2$ minor if and only if it has an edge. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_two_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 2)) G ↔ ∃ v w, G.Adj v w := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, -, -, hadj⟩
    obtain ⟨v, -, w, -, hvw⟩ := hadj 0 1 (by decide)
    exact ⟨v, w, hvw⟩
  · rintro ⟨v, w, hvw⟩
    refine ⟨![{v}, {w}], fun i => by fin_cases i <;> simp, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro i j hij
      fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [hvw.ne, hvw.ne.symm]
    · intro i j hij
      fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [hvw.symm]

/-- A graph with fewer than `t` vertices has no `K_t` minor. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem not_isMinor_completeGraph_of_card_lt [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) {t : ℕ}
    (ht : Fintype.card V < t) : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G := by
  rintro ⟨B, hconn, hdisj, -⟩
  have hne : ∀ i, (B i).Nonempty := fun i =>
    Set.nonempty_coe_sort.mp (hconn i).nonempty
  choose f hf using hne
  have hinj : Function.Injective f := fun i j hij => by
    by_contra hne
    exact Set.disjoint_left.mp (hdisj hne) (hf i) (hij ▸ hf j)
  have := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hinj
  simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at this
  omega

/--
**Hadwiger conjecture.** For every finite loopless graph $G$ and every positive integer $t$, if
$G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$.

Equivalently, if every proper coloring of $G$ uses at least $k$ colors, then $G$ contains $k$
pairwise disjoint connected subgraphs such that each pair of them is joined by an edge, i.e. $G$
has a $K_k$ minor. In algebraic form: $\chi(G) \le h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of
$G$ (the largest $k$ such that $K_k$ is a minor of $G$).

A `SimpleGraph` is loopless by definition, and parallel edges affect neither the chromatic number
nor the existence of a $K_t$ minor. The case $t = 0$ is degenerate: $K_0$ is a minor of every
graph (`isMinor_completeGraph_zero`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (hG : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) : G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture2

items: The list entry is terse; the precise formulation is taken from the first sentence of the linked article: 'if G is loopless and has no K_t minor then χ(G) < t'. Formalized in exactly that direction with a strict inequality; the equivalent forms (contrapositive, χ(G) ≤ h(G)) are only described in the docstring, not stated separately, per the decomposition table.

Graphs are Mathlib SimpleGraphs, which are loopless by definition. Wikipedia's 'loopless' allows multigraphs with parallel edges, but parallel edges change neither the chromatic number nor the existence of a K_t minor, so restricting to simple graphs loses nothing.
Finiteness is imposed via [Fintype V] on a universe-polymorphic vertex type, as the decomposition notes require and as is standard in the repository's graph files.

No hypothesis 0 < t is included. With the branch-set definition, K_0 is a minor of every graph (proved as isMinor_completeGraph_zero), so the t = 0 instance of the theorem is vacuous and the statement is logically equivalent to the one restricted to t ≥ 1 (Wikipedia's range 1 ≤ t ≤ 6 for the known cases). This is explained in the theorem docstring.

Minor containment is defined with 'at least one edge between adjacent branch sets' (rather than 'iff'), which is the correct ∃-characterization of 'H is a minor of G' since minors allow edge deletion; for H = K_t the two coincide anyway.

The bespoke definition lives in the problem file because the sandbox permits writing only candidate.lean; in a real PR it would arguably belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/ as a reusable definition (with its API lemmas), and a reviewer may wish to move it.

An additional research-solved variant hadwiger_conjecture_2.variants.le_six records the known cases t ≤ 6 (Wagner 1937 for t = 5 via the four color theorem; Robertson–Seymour–Thomas 1993 for t = 6), with a sorry proof body as the repo allows for informally established results.
